_comment: Accepted hardcoded-render-default findings (Gate B). Each entry is a pre-existing F3 violation accepted as layout debt. To FIX: replace the literal with var(--sgs-x, <default>) OR read the attr in render.php and emit it dynamically, then delete the baseline entry. To accept a NEW intentional hardcode: add an entry manually with a reason — do NOT re-run --write-baseline (it overwrites ALL accepted reasons).

accepted.reason: 2026-10-06 triage: not a defect. `brand-strip/style.css::.sgs-brand-strip__name` declares `line-height: 1.3` at (0,1,0) as the no-customisation baseline. `brand-strip/render.php` emits the real control on the SAME element with `sgs_typography_css_rule( $attributes, 'name', "{$root_sel} .sgs-brand-strip__name" )`, where `$root_sel = '.' . $uid . '.wp-block-sgs-brand-strip'`, so it lands at (0,3,0) and wins. E14 (`classifyInheritedHardcode`) classifies the declaration CLASS 1 (same element, not a finding). The legacy E11 branch of `scanCssDeclarations` reports it only because `selectorReferencesGovernedToken` compares class names and ignores specificity. Retire this entry when E11 is made specificity-aware.

2026-10-06 triage: not a defect. `button/style.css::.sgs-button` declares `line-height: 1.2` at (0,1,0) as the no-customisation baseline. `button/render.php` emits the real control on the SAME element with `sgs_typography_css_rule( $attributes, '', ".{$uid}.sgs-button" )`, where `$uid = 'sgs-btn-' . substr( md5( ... ), 0, 8 )` is a class, so it lands at (0,2,0) and wins. E14 (`classifyInheritedHardcode`) classifies the declaration CLASS 1 (same element, not a finding). The legacy E11 branch of `scanCssDeclarations` reports it only because `selectorReferencesGovernedToken` compares class names and ignores specificity. Retire this entry when E11 is made specificity-aware.

2026-10-06 triage: real gap, and the attribute named here is the wrong one. The rule is `mega-panel/style.css::.wp-block-sgs-mega-panel[ data-mega-style='cards' ] .sgs-mega-group { padding: 17px }`, the group card (child block `sgs/mega-group`), not the panel that `panelPadding` governs (`$panel_padding_obj` in `mega-panel/render.php`). Neither `mega-panel/block.json` (only `drawerCardPadding`, for the drawer) nor `mega-group/block.json` (`url`, `opensInNewTab`, `rel`) declares a card padding attribute, so the card padding has no inspector control. `mega-panel/render.php` repeats the literal in `$css .= $style_crd . $rel_group . '{padding:17px;border-radius:15px;...}'`, which the gate cannot see. Fix: add a card padding control and read it in both places.

2026-10-06 triage: real gap, and the attribute named here is the wrong one. The rule is `mega-panel/style.css::.wp-block-sgs-mega-panel[ data-mega-style='cards' ] .sgs-mega-group { border-radius: 15px }`, the group card (child block `sgs/mega-group`). `borderRadius` governs the panel root (`$border_radius` in `mega-panel/render.php`); the only card radius control is `drawerCardRadius`, for the drawer. The cards-style group card has no radius control. `mega-panel/render.php` repeats the literal in `$css .= $style_crd . $rel_group . '{padding:17px;border-radius:15px;...}'`, which the gate cannot see. Fix: add a card radius control and read it in both places.

2026-10-06 triage: not a defect. `product-card/style.css::.product-card` (the block root, `$classes = array( 'product-card' )`) declares `border-radius: 16px` at (0,1,0) as the no-customisation baseline. `borderRadius` is emitted on the SAME element by `wp_style_engine_get_styles( $sgs_pc_style_engine_args, array( 'selector' => $sgs_pc_root_sel ) )` with `$sgs_pc_root_sel = '.' . $sgs_card_uid . '.wp-block-sgs-product-card'` at (0,2,0), which wins. The attributes listed in `attr` (`pickerPillBorderRadius`, `pickerPillSelectedBorderRadius`, `tagBorderRadius`) are name-suffix collisions on other elements; `borderRadius` is the governing one.

accepted.attr: titleColour (default flattens headingLevel's theme-differentiated color across h2/h3/h4/h5/h6/p)
accepted.reason: 2026-08-17 — NOT a real F3 violation: the block.json default is a design-token SLUG, not a literal CSS colour. The F3b default-value scan reads it as a literal because isLiteralConstant()/formatDefaultForLiteralCheck() do not recognise a bare colour-token slug as var()-bound, while render.php only ever paints it as var(--wp--preset--color--<slug>), so the painted value follows each client's palette. Verified directly: render.php:99-104 declares a local `$colour_val` closure that always returns `var(--wp--preset--color--<slug>)`, and render.php:534-535 is the only place titleColour is painted, always through that closure — the block.json default "text" is never emitted as a literal. Same root cause, same out-of-scope-for-E12 disposition.

accepted.attr: titleColour (default flattens headingLevel's theme-differentiated color across h2/h3/h4/h5/h6/p)
accepted.reason: 2026-08-17 — same false-positive class as the sgs/pricing-table titleColour entry above (see that entry for the mechanism). Verified directly: render.php:381-382 paints titleColour exclusively through sgs_colour_value(), which returns 'var(--wp--preset--color--text)', never the literal 'text'. Same root cause, same out-of-scope-for-E12 disposition.

2026-10-06 triage: not a defect. `button/style.css::.sgs-button` declares `padding: 14px 24px` at (0,1,0) as the no-customisation baseline. When the author sets `padding`, `button/render.php` emits it on the SAME element with `wp_style_engine_get_styles( $base_style_engine_args, array( 'selector' => ".{$uid}.sgs-button" ) )` at (0,2,0), which wins. Padding is not an inherited property, so E14 does not audit it; this verdict comes from reading both selectors.

2026-10-06 triage: real gap, and the attributes named here govern other elements. The rule is `form/style.css::.sgs-form-tile { padding: 1rem }`, the tile label emitted by `form-field-tiles/render.php` (`<label class="sgs-form-tile" ...>`). `padding` governs the form root, `submitPadding` the submit button and `fieldPadding` the inputs (`$sgs_field_sel` in `form/render.php`); no attribute pads the tile (`form-field-tiles/block.json` declares only `gap` and `borderRadius` in this area). Padding is not inherited, so there is no leak. Fix: add a tile padding control.

2026-10-06 triage: not a defect. `heading/style.css::.wp-block-sgs-heading` declares `margin-bottom: 8px` at (0,1,0) as the no-customisation baseline (the file header says so). `heading/render.php` emits the real control on the SAME element: `$root_sel = '.' . $uid . '.wp-block-sgs-heading'` with `$uid = 'sgs-hdg-' . substr( md5( ... ), 0, 8 )`, carrying `margin` from `$base_margin_obj` at (0,2,0), which wins.

2026-10-06 triage: detector collision, not a real gap. `option-picker/style.css::.sgs-sr-only { margin: -1px }` is the standard visually-hidden recipe (`position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; ... margin: -1px`), used on `<legend id="%s" class="sgs-sr-only">` in `option-picker/render.php`. `isLiteralConstant` exempts `1px` on width and height but has no `-1px` margin case, so the recipe is checked against the block's `margin`. No attribute should own it.

2026-10-06 triage: real gap, and the attribute named here governs a different element. The rule is `product-faq/style.css::.sgs-product-faq-item + .sgs-product-faq-item { margin-top: 8px }`, the spacing between items (child block `sgs/product-faq-item`). `margin` governs the product-faq root. Neither `product-faq/block.json` nor `product-faq-item/block.json` declares an item gap or margin attribute, so the item spacing has no inspector control. Fix: add an item gap control to `sgs/product-faq`.

2026-10-06 triage: detector collision, not a real gap. `whatsapp-cta/style.css::.sgs-sr-only { margin: -1px }` is the standard visually-hidden recipe, used on `<span class="sgs-sr-only">` in `whatsapp-cta/render.php`. `isLiteralConstant` has no `-1px` margin case, so the recipe is checked against the block's `margin`. No attribute should own it.

2026-09-12 - detector collision, not a real gap: this rule (.sgs-nav-drawer__close svg) sizes the CLOSE ICON GLYPH, a completely different thing from the button BOX that closeSize governs (render.php's new closeSize CSS targets .sgs-nav-drawer__close, never its child svg). The close element's attrMap declares css:width/css:height -> closeSize for the button box (mirrors nav-menu's burgerSize); the detector's element-level match flags every width/height rule under that element's selector prefix, including this unrelated descendant. No attribute should own the icon's own fixed 28px render size.
2026-09-12 - same detector collision as the width:28px sibling entry above (.sgs-nav-drawer__close svg icon glyph size, not the closeSize-governed button box).
